about.title: Kerman Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Kerman is a small farm town west of Fresno, and most everyday errands happen along a handful of streets, with Madera Avenue, Whitesbridge Road, and California Avenue among them. Groceries, a hardware run, a stop at the pharmacy: those are also the places where a wet entryway, a broken curb, or an unlit stairwell can put someone on the ground without warning. Property owners in California owe visitors reasonable care. That does not make every fall a claim, though. The injured person usually has to show the owner knew about the hazard, or reasonably should have known, and still failed to fix it or post a warning. Proving that notice is where these cases are decided, and it depends heavily on evidence gathered early: photos of the exact spot, names of anyone who saw it, and the store or complex's surveillance footage before it gets recorded over. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Kerman residents free of charge with an independent attorney who takes premises cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Kerman Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Attorneys who know how to prove notice
items.desc: California requires showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network focus on locking down inspection logs, prior complaints, and video that establish exactly that.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most California premises claims carry a two-year filing limit, but falls on public property come with a much shorter claim window. An early connection helps make sure nothing lapses.

items.title: Partial fault is not a dead end
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so a claim can move forward even if you share some blame. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage, not erased.

items.question: I fell inside a store on Madera Avenue in Kerman. What should I do right now?
items.answer: Get medical care first, then ask the manager to write up an incident report and request that they preserve any surveillance footage of the area. Photograph the hazard, your footwear, and the surroundings before anything is cleaned up or fixed. Collect names and numbers of anyone who saw the fall, and keep the shoes you were wearing.

items.question: What if I tripped on a sidewalk or in a public building in Kerman?
items.answer: Claims against a city, county, or other public entity in California follow different rules, and the window to file a formal government claim is generally six months rather than two years. Missing that step can end the case before it starts. That is why it matters to sort out who owns or controls the property quickly.

items.question: I was looking at my phone when I slipped. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California applies pure comparative fault, so a court or insurer may assign you a share of responsibility, but that only reduces your recovery in proportion. The owner's duty to address a known hazard does not disappear because a visitor was distracted.
